body:
That is a good point! Proper testing is a major part of Software Engineering. Albeit it feels a bit neglected sometimes.
Maybe because it can feel overwhelming at first.

I can imagine that most beginners look for a simple tutorial to get a basic grip of the framework.
Including tests in ToH might seem out of the blue, unrelated and "too much" considering that the topic spans multiple pages (see screenshot below).

![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23424538/87398530-46287e00-c5b6-11ea-9e7b-82088958edf0.png)

That's just my opinion though. I'm happy to participate in the discussion and help out with a PR if we somehow go for it.
Maybe small notification/info box at the bottom of the page, instructing how to fix the tests would be enough? :)

That's a great idea for execution! I personally still think it might seem a out of place though. Testing is not mentioned nor covered in the whole series. Maybe we could use your idea to provide small testing bits throughout the lessons.

We should definetly consult someone senior like @kapunahelewong or @jbogarthyde :)

PS: Is Brandon Roberts still associated with the Docs?

How many other tutorials are there, apart from "Tour of heros"? @kapunahelewong or @jbogarthyde 

I'm a TDD/tests enthusiasth myself, and it really bothers me that the tutorials ends in applications with failing tests. If there are less than 5-6 tutorials, I am willing to accept the responsibility of adapting the tests and suggesting my contrubution to the tutorials as PRs with the descriptions on how to make them pass.

Or, perhaps an additional tutorial on how to test components all together.

This is such a helpful thread! And, as you two noticed, the testing info is undergoing some re-thinking. 

Regarding the tutorials, we are in the process of identifying tutorials throughout the docs and moving them into a new tutorials section. Sometimes, it's a little bit tricky because some of the current documentation has conceptual information  mixed in with longer tutorials. Because of this, you'll see some things being moved and then after the move someone goes in to sort out the actual content with a finer approach. We are doing it this way so that we can really see what's present in the docs and what we need to add, or in some cases clear out. We're also trying to keep docs PR scope really focused, so that's why you'll see incremental PRs.

cc @aikidave, our docs team lead for more context. 🌟

@s-gbz, regarding your question, Brandon has since left the docs and I miss him!

@kapunahelewong, as is so often the case, correct! 

I think adding testing to tour of heroes (and maybe the stackblitz-based tutorial as well?) would be a great thing to do. @Danon, I think both of your ideas are good: making sure the tests pass(!) and also looking into adding additional tutorials on testing. What's the best way for us to connect to discuss this further?

@kapunahelewong I am happy to see you appreciate the value of common contribution as well as proper TDD!

I am available on Discord and Google Meets, but I can also join other media of communication. 

As of me, I've been working with Vue and React/Jsx a lot lately (something like 2 years), but did have had angular at the back of my head often. Now, that I've tried it, I see its value more and more - Yes, it does require more effort to start, but it offers much more and I feel, it is (in comparison) much more mature.

In addition, I'm a TDD enthusiast, and I have a quiet feeling that Angular maintainers and doc authors are too, that's why I'm more than happy to contribute and suggest ideas.
